title: eval-harness: add per-prompt-set regression CI gate and quality thresholds
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Adds per-prompt-set CI gating to detect prompt regressions; integrates new quality metrics into CI and surfaces failures to Slack; includes migration notes for existing prompt sets.
description: Motivation: We have seen intermittent regressions caused by prompt-set drift and model switches that slip past global eval metrics. This PR implements a per-prompt-set regression gate in the CI pipeline so failures are caught close to the source. What it does: 1) Adds per-prompt-set thresholds (precision/recall/utility) computed by the eval harness; 2) Extends CI pipeline to run targeted evals for changed prompt sets and fail the job on threshold violations; 3) Adds a lightweight Slack notifier with failure context and links to failing prompt examples; 4) Adds a docs page describing the gate and migration steps. Checklist: - [x] Implement metric computation hooks and threshold config - [x] Wire gate into CI pipeline (ci/pipelines/eval-gate.yml) - [x] Add tests for metric edgecases and gating logic - [x] Add Slack notifier and templates - [x] Documentation and migration notes Why now: teams are onboarding multiple open models with different quality characteristics; catching prompt-specific regressions earlier reduces production incidents and rollback churn. Backwards compatibility: default thresholds are conservative and can be overridden per-prompt-set via prompt_set.yaml. Rollout plan: stage the gate on the integration branch for two weeks with notifications only, then flip to blocking after stakeholder signoff.
